name: Head Pose Estimation v2
description: Analyzes head pose physics and rotation to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Head Pose Estimation v2 — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method performs advanced head pose analysis for deepfake detection:

1. **6-DOF Pose Estimation**: Head pose is estimated with 6 degrees of freedom (3D rotation: yaw, pitch, roll + 3D translation) per frame using a combination of facial landmarks and perspective-n-point (PnP) solving with a 3D face model.

2. **Pose Trajectory Smoothness**: Head pose trajectories should be smooth (low jerk), reflecting the biomechanical properties of the cervical spine and head mass. The method analyzes trajectory smoothness using third-derivative (jerk) metrics. Deepfakes may produce jittery pose trajectories from frame-independent head estimation.

3. **Geometric Self-Consistency**: The estimated 3D pose should be geometrically self-consistent: (a) reprojected landmark positions should match detected landmarks, (b) face visibility should be consistent with estimated pose, (c) facial feature foreshortening should match perspective projection at the estimated pose. Deepfakes may show geometric inconsistencies.

4. **Pose-Dependent Face Appearance**: At different head poses, different face surfaces become visible. The method checks whether newly visible regions (revealed during head rotation) are consistent with previously visible regions — same texture quality, same skin tone, same detail level. Deepfakes may show inconsistent face appearance as pose changes reveal poorly generated regions.

5. **Pose Range Analysis**: The range of head poses in the video is analyzed. Natural head movement in conversation typically stays within ±30° yaw, ±20° pitch. The method checks whether deepfake quality degrades at extreme poses (common for face-swap models trained primarily on frontal faces), creating a detectable pose-dependent artifact signature.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through head pose estimation v2 analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Yang, X. et al. (2019). Exposing Deep Fakes Using Inconsistent Head Poses. ICASSP.
